subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these fourteen third-party GitHub Action revisions, including the `openai/codex-action` and GitHub App token action updates, for credentialed repository workflows?
rationale: The patch preserves full commit-SHA pinning and does not change workflow permissions, but accepting new executable third-party revisions in secret-bearing automation is a trust-boundary decision that cannot be resolved from version churn alone.

options.title: Approve vetted revisions
options.body: Verify the upstream action revisions and their release contracts, then merge the refreshed head after required checks pass.

options.title: Hold the Codex update
options.body: Ask for a narrowly scoped revision that excludes `openai/codex-action` until its exact action contract has been reviewed.

options.title: Close and regenerate later
options.body: Close this Dependabot batch if maintaining a fourteen-action bundle is not worth the current trust-review cost; a later update can be reviewed as a fresh head.

recommendation.title: Approve vetted revisions
recommendation.body: Verify the upstream action revisions and their release contracts, then merge the refreshed head after required checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: A workflow or security owner is needed, but the available context does not safely identify a specific individual.
